title: PT Rejects Rupture With Morena; “We Will Always Go With the President,” Alberto Anaya Says
author: Alma E. Muñoz and Emir Olivares
content:
_This article by[Alma E. Muñoz and Emir
Olivares](https://www.jornada.com.mx/autores/Alma%20E.%20Mu%C3%B1oz%20y%20Emir%20Olivares)
originally appeared in the [September 27, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/09/27/politica/no-va-a-haber-
ruptura-asegura-el-pt-sobre-la-alianza-con-morena-rumbo-a-proximas-
elecciones), Mexico's premier left wing daily newspaper._

**Mexico City**. With Morena there will be no rupture; "we will always go with
the president (Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo), we will always go in coalition,"
asserted the leader of the Labor Party (PT), Alberto Anaya.

On his arrival at the capital's Zócalo, to take part in the president's last
accountability report on her year in office, he stated in a brief interview
that **everything is going well at the negotiating table on the 2027 electoral
process** that they maintain with Morena's leadership.

He said that making public the results of the polls for coordinators of the
transformation in the states "is part of an agreed procedure."

"There will be no rupture?" he was asked.

"Of course not; we have no reason to, we love the president very much, we have
to close ranks with her," he stressed.

### "We Are in the Same Project": Miriam Saldaña

"There is not going to be a rupture" with Morena, affirmed this morning the
vice coordinator of the Labor Party (PT) caucus in the Mexico City Congress,
Miriam Saldaña, who is also a member of the national coordination of that
political organization.

She said that the PT coordinating table, which is negotiating to maintain the
alliance with Morena, has already informed them that there will be no break.
This despite **threats by leaders of that party to suspend the alliance due to
their disagreement over the selection of the state coordinators of the 4T**.

![Miriam Saldaña near the Zócalo of Mexico
City](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/02-miriam-
saldana.jpg)Miriam Saldaña, vice coordinator of the Labor Party (PT) caucus,
near the Zócalo of Mexico City to witness President Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo's
accountability report. Photo: video screenshot, Alma E. Muñoz

"There is a specialized team for the elections table and I think it is
advancing very well. **We are definitely in the same project: the 4T, and we
must stay together.**

"There is not going to be a rupture, there are always these kinds of scrapes
in any negotiation, but we have to come to an agreement, because going
together is how we are going to make the transformation happen," she asserted
in an interview on her arrival to join the event at which President Claudia
Sheinbaum will present her accountability report in the country's capital.

She stated that the negotiating table has informed PT members about the
progress and everything points to the alliance being maintained.

Separately, the spokesperson for the Morena caucus in the Chamber of Deputies,
Arturo Ávila, guaranteed that the union of both political organizations will
be maintained.

> Of course there will be an alliance with the PT and the Green Party. Those
> of us who are in this project are here for the tasks, not for the posts.
>
> Arturo Ávila, Morena spokesperson in the Chamber of Deputies

He floated Citlalli Hernández, current president of the Elections Commission
of Morena's leadership, as a possible coordinator of the movement to head the
candidacy for the Cuauhtémoc borough, in Mexico City, which is currently
governed by the opposition.
